name: Sleeper Stretch
steps: Lie on your target side with your head comfortably supported by a pillow.
Extend your target upper arm straight out in front of your shoulder at a 90-degree angle, with your elbow bent at 90 degrees pointing your fingers toward the ceiling.
Roll your body slightly backward (about 20 degrees) so you are resting on the back of your shoulder blade, not directly on the shoulder joint.
Use your opposite hand to gently guide the wrist of your target arm downward toward the floor.
Stop at the first sensation of a gentle stretch deep in the back of your shoulder and hold for 20 to 30 seconds.
coaching_cues: Apply very gentle, steady pressure with your top hand; never force the wrist down or push through sharp pain.
The stretch should be felt in the back of the shoulder capsule, never in the front.
Breathe slowly and deeply to help the posterior rotator cuff relax.

sources.attribution: Cornell Health Shoulder Range of Motion Protocol
